title: Heavy work offloads to the cluster by default (build/verify/lanes)
content: Heavy blackbox work offloads to the operator's cluster BY DEFAULT: interactive heavy worktrees come from the warm-standby lane pool, `~/repos/bbox-cage/build/lanes/lane-pool.sh claim` (sub-second; prints the checkout path; `release <name>` when done), falling back to `bin/estate lane create <name> --family bbox` from the operator's estate root for a named lane (~5 min to full warmth); full verification via `~/repos/bbox-cage/build/submit-bbox-verify.sh --ref <ref>`; linux/amd64 images via `~/repos/bbox-cage/build/submit-bbox-build.sh`. cargo/rustc/sccache route into the lane pod keyed on cwd; read `~/repos/bbox-cage/build/lanes/BBOX_LANE_WORK.md` before heavy work; worker loss is lane loss, push durable work. Local stays: file edits, single-crate check/test loops, and the arm64 macOS daemon build/deploy. PROJECT.md 'Where Heavy Work Runs' is the full contract; contributors without the estate fall back to the plain local gates.
rationale: Operator approved verbatim (bbox-build-cluster session, 2026-07-18): agents must reach for cluster-backed tooling by default.
